title: Self-Cleaning Cycle Error
shortDescription: Salt chlorinator cell reversing polarity issue.
fullDescription:
SC indicates an issue during the self-cleaning (polarity reversal) cycle of the AquaRite salt cell. Often a relay or drive issue.

May need control board service.

title: Flow Switch Open
shortDescription: Flow switch reports no flow through cell.
fullDescription:
Flow switch detects inadequate water flow through the chlorinator cell. Pump must run; often caused by dirty filter or closed valves.

Check pump operation and filter condition.

fixSteps.title: Check pump
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure pump runs and flow is good.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: If flow OK, replace flow switch.

title: Pressure Sensor Error
fullDescription: Hayward heater E01 indicates pressure switch open (low flow) or sensor error. Check filter and valves.

fixSteps.title: Check flow
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure pump running strong and filter clean.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: If flow OK, replace pressure switch.

title: Low Salt Level
fullDescription:
Salt level below 2700 ppm. Cell cannot produce chlorine efficiently. Add salt per calculator.

Test salt with strips and add pool salt, not water softener salt.

fixSteps.title: Add salt
fixSteps.instruction: Add per Hayward calculator. Typical 3200 ppm.

fixSteps.title: Clean cell
fixSteps.instruction: If reading low but tests OK, acid wash cell.

title: High Salt Level
fullDescription:
Salt level above 3800 ppm. Too much salt can damage the cell and is corrosive.

Dilute pool by partial drain and refill.

fixSteps.title: Partial drain
fixSteps.instruction: Drain and refill to reduce salt.

whenToCallPro: If unsure how much to drain.

title: No Water Flow
shortDescription: No flow detected at salt cell.
fullDescription:
E08 signals no flow in the cell. Pump must run and flow must be adequate.

Check pump, filter, and flow switch.

title: No Cell Detected
shortDescription: Salt cell not connected or unrecognized.
fullDescription:
E09 means controller isn't reading the salt cell. Cable disconnect, cell failure, or wrong cell type.

Check cable and verify cell model matches setup.

fixSteps.title: Check cable
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect and reseat cell cable at both ends.

fixSteps.title: Replace cell
fixSteps.instruction: If 3-5 years old, likely end of life.

videoSearchQuery: Hayward AquaRite E09 no cell detected

title: Cell Voltage Error
fullDescription:
Abnormal cell voltage. Usually cold water, low salt, scaled cell, or end of life.

Check water temp, salt level, and inspect cell.

fixSteps.title: Check temp
fixSteps.instruction: Normal below 60°F; wait for warmer water.

title: Flow Error / Fault
shortDescription: Flow sensor fault on heater or chlorinator.
fullDescription:
FE indicates the flow sensor reading is outside expected range or has failed.

Check pump and filter; replace sensor if needed.

faq.a: Similar; FE can indicate sensor hardware fault.

title: Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Water temperature sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription:
ST means water temp sensor is not reading correctly. Usually bad sensor, wire, or connector corrosion.

Replace the sensor.

faq.a: Yes, stocked at pool supply stores.
